findings.name: cherry-picked-baseline
findings.location: Section 'Classical Baselines' and 'Results: Ideal versus Noisy Quantum Kernels'
findings.evidence: We compared against the following classical kernel methods: (i) Radial basis function (RBF) kernel... (ii) Polynomial kernel... (iii) Random Fourier features (RFF) kernel approximation... (iv) Classical simulation of ideal quantum kernel via statevector computation.
findings.suggested_fix: Include state-of-the-art classical methods for each task: neural network baselines for parity learning, GNNs for molecular property prediction, and equivariant neural networks for symmetry datasets.

findings.name: conflated-regimes
findings.evidence: Then there exist data distributions $\mathcal{D}$ such that the quantum kernel effective dimension satisfies $d_{\text{eff}}^Q(\lambda) = \Omega(2^{n/2})$... These requirements represent a factor of $<$INSERT MEASURED VALUE$>\times$ improvement over current median device performance
findings.suggested_fix: Add finite-size scaling analysis computing theoretical effective dimension ratios at actual tested qubit counts and acknowledge exponential separation may not manifest at small scales.

findings.name: asymptotic-only-claim
findings.evidence: $d_{\text{eff}}^Q(\lambda) = \Omega(2^{n/2})$ for $\lambda = \mathcal{O}(1/\text{poly}(n))$, while any classical kernel computable in time $\text{poly}(n)$ has effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}^C(\lambda) = \mathcal{O}(\text{poly}(n))$
findings.suggested_fix: Provide explicit non-asymptotic bounds at tested qubit counts, or clearly state theorem provides asymptotic guarantees only and experiments are preliminary validation at pre-asymptotic scales.

findings.name: active-space-handwave
findings.evidence: Development of problem-specific quantum feature maps that maximize the alignment between task structure and quantum kernel geometry while minimizing required circuit depth
findings.suggested_fix: Test on additional diverse real-world datasets or explicitly scope conclusions to the specific tested benchmarks without generalizing language.

findings.name: hardware-irrelevant-comparison
findings.location: Results Section, 'Results: Ideal versus Noisy Quantum Kernels'
findings.evidence: ideal quantum kernels achieved test accuracy of $<$INSERT MEASURED VALUE$>$\%... compared to $<$INSERT MEASURED VALUE$>$\% for the best classical baseline
findings.suggested_fix: Make noisy-hardware-vs-classical the primary comparison for advantage claims; report ideal quantum only as upper bound to contextualize noise degradation.

findings.name: hasty-generalization
findings.evidence: Our finding that classification accuracy degrades sharply when $\Delta_\kappa$ exceeds approximately $<$INSERT MEASURED VALUE$>$ establishes a concrete target for hardware developers
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify that the threshold derives from only three specific datasets and may vary for different task structures and feature maps.

findings.name: circular-reasoning
findings.evidence: This confirms the theoretical expectation that parity-like functions align well with quantum kernel geometry.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe as validation of implementation on a dataset constructed to favor quantum kernels, not independent evidence of practical advantage.

findings.name: affirming-the-consequent
findings.evidence: Theorems~\ref{thm:separation} and~\ref{thm:generalization} together establish that quantum kernels can achieve better generalization than classical kernels when the learning problem structure aligns with the quantum feature map geometry
findings.suggested_fix: Add analysis showing full generalization bound (including dual variable norms and margins) favors quantum kernels, or weaken claim to 'may achieve better generalization under specific additional conditions.'
